description: Mongol successor state in Central Asia (1226–1347) established by Chagatai Khan, second son of Genghis Khan; controlled the heartland of Transoxiana and the Tarim Basin; internal conflict between nomadic and settled factions led to its fragmentation and eventual replacement by the Timurid Empire.

temporal.notes: Founded by Chagatai Khan; split into eastern (Moghulistan) and western (Transoxiana) halves c.1334; western half conquered by Timur by 1370

lifecycle_phases.description: Chagatai Khan rules as loyal subordinate to the Great Khan; administers Central Asian heartland; court maintains nomadic traditions while administering settled Transoxiana through Persian bureaucrats
Khanate divided between pro-nomadic factions favoring Mongolian steppe lifestyle and pro-settled factions seeking to embrace Persian-Islamic civilization; persistent succession wars
Khan Kebek builds permanent capital at Qarshi; monetary reforms; partial Islamization; eastern territories remain nomadic; Black Death and Timur's rise end Chagatai power

rise_factors.description: Chagatai's status as son of Genghis Khan gave the khanate unquestioned legitimacy among Mongol tribes; the Silk Road heartland was the wealthiest inheritance in the Mongol partition
Control of Transoxiana and the Tarim Basin gave the Chagatai Khanate revenues from the most trafficked section of the overland Silk Road connecting China to the Middle East
Positioned between the Ilkhanate, Golden Horde, and Yuan Dynasty, Chagatai khans could play rivals against each other and extract concessions from all three

decline_factors.description: Fundamental tension between nomadic Mongol identity and the need to govern settled Persian-speaking cities produced repeated civil wars that prevented stable institutions
Timur (Tamerlane), a Barlas Turco-Mongol from Transoxiana, progressively absorbed Chagatai territory from 1360 onward, culminating in control of all former Chagatai lands by 1380
The plague devastated trade-dependent Central Asian cities in the 1340s, collapsing the Silk Road revenues that sustained the khanate

sources.author: Manz, Beatrice Forbes
sources.title: The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane
